The world's biggest PC maker just saw its worst growth in over two years.
Lenovo said Wednesday that revenue stood at almost $17 billion for the April to June quarter.
That was up just 0.2% on a year earlier.
Lenovo has seen PC demand cool after a lockdown-driven surge.
Its shipments of the devices were down almost 13% according to researchers at CounterPoint.
However, it held onto top spot among PC makers, with almost a quarter share of the market.
The cooling demand for new devices has sparked warnings from firms including Intel and Samsung.
Makers have also faced headaches as a result of fresh lockdowns in China, which disrupted production.
However, Lenovo is enjoying a boom in demand for gadgets besides PCs.
Its revenue from smartphone sales was up by more than a fifth on the year.
The firm has also been targeting servers and information technology services.
Lenovo's Hong Kong-traded shares closed the day down around 2%.
From US to China, still there is no relief for citizens of the country from the price rise.
Latest data shows China's consumer inflation has accelerated in July to highest level in two years.
This after world's second largest economy is easing rules after observing strict lockdowns.
On the incidence of rising COVID cases in the country, this has complicated nations' efforts to get its COVID-hit economy back on track with more stimulus.
Now, according to data released this morning, consumer price index CPI was up 2.7% last month from last year.
It has missed economists' expectations of 2.9% gain.
It is strongest pace since July of 2020 and compares with 2.5% growth in June.
However, reports also say that in contrast to other major economies,
consumer inflation in China has been relatively subdued this year
as strict COVID control policies and outbreaks has curbed consumer and business spending there.
China has set consumer inflation target of around 3% for the whole of this year.
